title: Identification in Missing-Not-at-Random Graphs on Structural Support Faces
banked_reason: The promised support-aware formula-or-exact-twin resolution is not delivered: the theorem permits UNRESOLVED, leaves all 594 residual pairs unclassified, and does not prove the required DAG or ADMG completeness/deformation result.
gap_reasons: The promised support-aware formula-or-exact-twin resolution is not delivered: this theorem deliberately permits UNRESOLVED, and oeq:dag-calculus-completeness and oeq:admg-support-completeness leave the required DAG converse and all ADMG completeness/deformation work open.
The three-output result proves neither the advertised formula-or-twins dichotomy nor a completeness certificate-size bound and leaves 594 cases without formulas, twins, or an executable ledger.
The accepted result class was materially substituted after its central obligations failed, so it is not merely below-floor.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a universal support-aware closure-or-deformation theorem for finite MNAR DAGs and ADMGs, including exact rational twins and bounded certificates. It established a sound partial calculus, support normalization, deterministic-parent deletion, and a verified 324-to-366 preprocessing gain, but the early-kill audit left all 594 residual binary faces unclassified and the calculus retained an UNRESOLVED branch. Universal DAG converse/rational-witness bounds and support-safe ADMG fixing completeness therefore remain open; the validity gate confirmed that narrowing the accepted promise after this failure would be laundering.
tldr: For finite discrete MNAR DAGs on a fixed support face, the support normal form validates the face, and an explicit simultaneous-deletion corollary proves that every substantive arrow into a response indicator with singleton support at each reachable local row may be removed at once without changing the model class. The finite procedure terminates with \(\mathtt{FORMULA}\), \(\mathtt{TWIN}\), or \(\mathtt{UNRESOLVED}\), with verifier-sound conclusions only for the first two outputs. In the audited binary census, deletion adds exactly \(42\) successes and loses none: compatible-face donor coverage rises from \(324/960=33.75\%\) to \(366/960=38.125\%\), an increase of \(4.375\) percentage points and approximately \(12.96\%\) relative to the original \(324\); all remaining \(594\) pairs are unclassified. Returned formula certificates compile to MISPR kernels. For ADMGs, each order has a finite denominator-survival test and boundary values agree when both orders pass that test; whether different orders pass on the same faces, a complete support-safe nested-fixing grammar, and completeness or deformation remain open.
gap: Strict-positive graphical completeness is known, and PM-ID+ is sound for sparse pattern support under P1 and P3, but no inspected source supplies arbitrary-support completeness, an explicit finite formula-or-twin grammar, or bounded exact negative certificates. In Phung et al. (2025), Section 3.3.2, Corollary 5 proves PM-ID soundness; Section 4.2.2, Corollary 9 proves PM-ID+ soundness; and Section 8 leaves PM-ID+ completeness open.
fill: Prove that the explicit R0-R6 grammar has no UNRESOLVED DAG output, with the stated circuit and rational-witness bounds; use the completed 594-pair audit as the first falsifiable base case; compile every FORMULA output into support-correct MISPR kernels; and investigate ADMGs only after a support-safe nested-fixing boundary lemma.
